summary.text: 床 is the popular form of 牀 that became standard. 牀 is traditionally analyzed as 木, a meaning element, plus 爿, a sound element; the proposal that 爿 depicts a bed remains uncertain.

formation.text: The historical graph 牀 is analyzed as phonosemantic: 木 contributes meaning and 爿 is assigned a phonetic role. A separate account interprets 爿 as a bed picture and proposes it as an early graph for bed, but its cited inscription use is glossed as a place name, so that interpretation remains uncertain.

components.text: In 牀, 木 is identified as the semantic element, linking the graph to resting furniture. This is a component of the historical graph, not current 床.

牀’s traditional analysis assigns 爿 a phonetic role. A separate account interprets an oracle-bone form as a bed picture and proposes 爿 as an early graph for bed; the cited inscription use is glossed as a place name.

sound_limitation.text: The word written 牀 has the Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction *k.dzraŋ, but this does not establish 爿’s pronunciation in its proposed phonetic role. The reported Zhengzhang form *zaŋ for 爿 is secondary and was not independently verified against that reconstruction system, so a same-system comparison is unavailable here.

history.text: 床 is recorded as a popular variant of 牀, and that popular form later became standard. The relationship is one of graphic variation, not evidence that 床 is an earlier form.

The curated Warring States bronze-style redraw shows 牀 with 木 and 爿; the oracle-bone-style redraw shows 爿 alone. These images illustrate forms discussed in historical accounts but do not establish a sequence of development.

uncertainties.text: The proposal that oracle-bone 爿 depicts a bed remains uncertain: its cited inscription use is glossed as a place name, and the account does not date that inscription. The chronology between 爿 and 牀 is unresolved.

The traditional analysis assigns 爿 a phonetic role in 牀, but the available sources do not provide an independently verified, same-system pronunciation comparison for 爿 in that role. The proposed bed object’s name or pronunciation is also unestablished.

senses.gloss: place for sitting or resting the body
senses.text: 牀 is glossed as a place for sitting or resting the body. The earliest securely dated witness for this sense is unresolved.
Bed and couch are documented meanings of 牀/床, but the earliest use of the bed word is not securely dated here.

senses.gloss: rack, support, base, or bed-like surface
senses.text: These meanings are recorded, but their dates and any path linking them to the resting-place sense are unresolved.
Classifier use is documented, but its development from another sense is not established.

limitations.text: Several meanings are documented, but the evidence does not establish when they arose or whether one developed from another, so no semantic links are asserted.
The proposed Khmer, Mon, Burmese, and Vietic comparisons do not establish a borrowing history for the Chinese word written 牀/床.

overview.text: 床 is the standard form of 牀, used for places to rest and for bed furniture. In 牀, 木 contributes meaning and 爿 is assigned a sound role, though its pronunciation in that role lacks an independently verified comparison.

components.text: In 牀, 木 links the graph with resting furniture; it belongs to the historical form, not current 床.
爿 is assigned a sound role in 牀. A separate proposal sees it as an early bed picture, but that interpretation is uncertain.

relationships.text: 床 is a popular variant of 牀 that later became standard; this does not establish it as an earlier form.
The historical analysis of 牀 identifies 木 as semantic; this role belongs to 牀, not automatically to current 床.
The traditional analysis of 牀 identifies 爿 as phonetic, although an independently verified pronunciation comparison for 爿 in that role is unavailable.
